ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Gated fusion of focus-axis and spatial features
PROPOSAL: Build a stack network on a DINOv2 small encoder with a slice-axis branch and a spatial branch over neighbouring pixels, merged by a learned gate that switches off texture gradients when the focus signal shows no peak shift. Train on FoD500 and DDFF 12-Scene with 5-slice stacks. Report RMSE, AbsRel, delta accuracy and an edge-precision score at true depth discontinuities.
CONTROLS: No gate; per-pixel argmax over a Laplacian focus measure; a plain 2D U-Net on channel-stacked slices; DFV of Yang et al. retrained on the same splits; 3 seeds.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: The gate lowers false edges on patterned surfaces relative to the ungated variant, with a modest RMSE gain. It could fail on reflective regions where the signal stays flat and gives the gate no peak to rely on.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Profile-shape transformer along the slice axis
PROPOSAL: Treat the focus profile of a pixel as a short sequence and encode it with a 1D transformer over DINOv2 large features, decoding depth with a lightweight 2D head. Train on FoD500 with 5-slice stacks, and evaluate RMSE, AbsRel and an abrupt-change score computed on pixels where ground-truth depth jumps across adjacent pixels, at the native resolution and at 2 downsampled ones, with the encoder frozen and unfrozen, using the sharpest-slice image as guide to the decoder.
CONTROLS: Mean pooling over slices; argmax of a Tenengrad measure; a 2D U-Net on channel-stacked slices with matched parameters; DFV retrained on the same splits; 3 seeds.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: The sequence encoder should localise the focus peak more precisely than pooling, mostly near depth jumps. It might fail where profiles are bimodal because two surfaces overlap inside a pixel.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Thin-lens re-rendering loss for label-free stack training
PROPOSAL: Train a ConvNeXt-T network without depth labels on DDFF 12-Scene and a smartphone focal sweep set, predicting depth and an all-in-focus image. Re-render the stack with a thin-lens circle-of-confusion model and penalise the mismatch against the slices, adding an image-gradient-weighted smoothness term only where the rendered focus peak is unambiguous. Evaluate RMSE and AbsRel on held-out scenes and on a low-texture subset of 40 stacks.
CONTROLS: A learned defocus renderer in place of the thin-lens model; no smoothness term; supervised DFV on the same scenes; a self-supervised baseline that reconstructs only the all-in-focus image; 5 seeds.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: The physical renderer should beat the learned one on the low-texture subset by a visible gap, since it cannot absorb errors into free parameters. It could fail on the smartphone sweeps if the lens calibration is off, which would appear as a scale bias in AbsRel.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Aperture-conditioned depth network trained on rendered stacks
PROPOSAL: Feed a Swin-B backbone the stack together with a 3-value aperture code, and train on DDFF 12-Scene alone with synthetic stacks re-rendered from its ground-truth depth at 4 aperture settings, to teach the network how defocus grows with distance from the focal plane. Evaluate RMSE and AbsRel on held-out scenes and on a low-texture subset of 40 stacks, and check whether error falls when the code supplied at inference matches the aperture used for rendering.
CONTROLS: Training on the original stacks only; a code-free variant; supervised DFV on the same scenes; Laplacian argmax; 3 seeds.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Rendered stacks should add robustness to aperture changes, although the benefit may shrink when the rendering model departs from the real lens. It could fail if the network ignores the code and relies on texture cues.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Texture versus depth-edge diagnostic for focus measures
PROPOSAL: Render focal stacks from NYU Depth v2 scenes with a thin-lens model and paste printed-pattern textures onto flat planes, so that strong gradients appear both with and without a true depth step. Train a 3-layer 3D CNN on 400 such stacks and compare it with Laplacian and Tenengrad measures followed by argmax and median smoothing. Report the false-edge rate on textured planes, the recall of true depth steps, and RMSE.
CONTROLS: Pattern frequency varied at 4 levels; a model trained on untextured renders only; a 2D CNN on the all-in-focus image alone; classical measures with tuned window sizes; 3 seeds.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Classical measures should produce false edges on high-frequency patterns at a much higher rate than the 3D CNN. The CNN could fail on patterns whose period matches the blur radius, where texture and defocus become hard to separate.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Planted false-edge test of learned and classical focus measures
PROPOSAL: Generate stacks procedurally from random planes and steps with 3 texture families (stripes, checkerboards, noise), render defocus with a thin-lens model, and score the methods on how often it reports a depth edge where none exists. The methods are Laplacian, Tenengrad and a ResNet-50 3D network trained on 2000 stacks drawn from FoD500 and DefocusNet scene layouts. Report false-edge rate, recall of true steps and RMSE on held-out layouts and held-out texture families.
CONTROLS: Pattern frequency at 4 levels; a model trained on untextured renders only; a 2D CNN on the all-in-focus image alone; window sizes of the classical measures tuned on a validation split; 10 seeds.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Learned networks should keep false edges low on stripes and checkerboards, while classical measures respond to any strong gradient. It could fail on noise textures, whose gradients look like genuine focus transitions.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Metric refinement of a relative-depth prior using focus cues
PROPOSAL: Take Depth Anything V2 small as a frozen relative-depth prior and learn a light focal-stack branch that predicts a per-pixel scale and shift from the focus profile, anchored by the sharpest-slice distance. Train on FoD500 and DDFF 12-Scene with stack lengths of 3, 5 and 9, and then evaluate metric RMSE and AbsRel, plus sharpness of depth edges measured by gradient error against ground truth.
CONTROLS: The prior alone with global least-squares alignment; the prior fine-tuned without stack input; the branch fed shuffled slice order; DFV retrained on the same splits; 3 seeds.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: The branch should remove most of the scale error left by global alignment and keep the prior's sharp edges. It could fail on scenes where the prior mis-orders objects, since focus cues fix scale but not ordering.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learned per-slice sharpness maps on a large encoder
PROPOSAL: Train a ViT-L encoder to predict a sharpness map of the slices in FoD500 stacks, supervised by synthetic Gaussian blur of known radius from 1 to 8 pixels, then read depth by soft-argmax over slices followed by a small refinement U-Net. Evaluate RMSE and AbsRel on the FoD500 evaluation set, with gradient error at ground-truth depth edges, with the encoder frozen and trained and over 3 radius ranges.
CONTROLS: Laplacian and Tenengrad response maps with soft-argmax; the refinement U-Net alone on the all-in-focus image; DFV retrained on the same splits; 5 seeds.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: Learned sharpness should locate the focus peak better than Laplacian on low-texture patches, since synthetic blur supervision does not depend on texture. It could fail to transfer from Gaussian blur to the real lens blur in FoD500.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Factorised spatial and focal attention for stack transformers
PROPOSAL: Design a transformer that alternates windowed attention across neighbouring pixels with attention across slices at quarter resolution, on a Swin-T encoder. Train on FoD500, DDFF 12-Scene and DefocusNet with 5-slice stacks, and evaluate RMSE, AbsRel and an abrupt-change score computed on pixels whose ground-truth depth jumps by more than 10 percent across neighbours.
CONTROLS: Joint space-slice attention of matched parameter count; spatial attention only on the sharpest slice; slice attention only; DFV retrained on the same splits; 5 seeds.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: Factorised attention should outperform the joint variant on the abrupt-change score while matching it on RMSE. It could fail if windowing breaks continuity across big flat regions, producing blocky depth.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Two-stream focus and appearance network with late fusion
PROPOSAL: Run a ViT-B stream on the sharpest-slice image and a Swin-B stream on the focus volume, and fuse them with cross-attention in the decoder, so appearance supplies object boundaries and the focus stream supplies scale. Train on FoD500 with 5-slice stacks and evaluate RMSE, AbsRel and an abrupt-change score on pixels whose ground-truth depth jumps by over 10 percent across neighbours, over 3 input resolutions.
CONTROLS: Appearance stream alone; focus stream alone; early fusion by channel concatenation with matched parameters; DFV retrained on the same splits; 3 seeds.
COST: 500
PREDICTION: Late fusion should recover sharp object boundaries that the focus stream alone blurs, with scale error close to that stream. It could fail if the appearance stream dominates and imports texture-induced edges.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Stack-length robustness through slice dropout training
PROPOSAL: Train a ViT-L based network with random slice dropout on FoD500, DDFF 12-Scene, DefocusNet and a smartphone focal sweep set, then test with 3, 5, 9 and 15 slices and with irregular focal spacing. Report RMSE and AbsRel against stack length, and the change in depth-edge sharpness when slices are removed. Use a focus-distance embedding so the network knows the spacing of its slices.
CONTROLS: Fixed-length training at 5 slices; training without the focus-distance embedding; classical Laplacian argmax; DFV retrained per stack length; 5 seeds.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Slice dropout should flatten the error curve against stack length, with the biggest gains at 3 slices. It could fail on the smartphone sweeps, whose focal spacing falls outside the training distribution.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distilling a long-stack teacher into short-stack students
PROPOSAL: Train a ViT-L teacher on 15-slice FoD500 stacks and distil it into students that see 3, 5 or 9 slices by matching depth maps and intermediate focus features. Report RMSE and AbsRel against stack length on held-out stacks, and the change in depth-edge sharpness from teacher to student, including irregular focal spacing for the students.
CONTROLS: Students trained from labels only; students trained with slice dropout; classical Laplacian argmax; DFV retrained per stack length; 3 seeds.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Distillation should close most of the gap to the teacher at 9 slices and less at 3. It could fail if the teacher's errors on fine texture are copied into the students.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Ambiguity head for reflective and low-texture regions
PROPOSAL: Add a confidence head to a ViT-L network, trained to predict the entropy of the per-pixel focus profile from the stack itself, and then use it to flag pixels with ambiguous responses. Build a reflective subset of 200 stacks from DDFF 12-Scene frames carrying specular masks, and a low-texture subset from FoD500, with 5-slice stacks. Report selective-prediction curves, with RMSE as a function of the fraction of pixels kept, on both subsets.
CONTROLS: Confidence taken from the Laplacian response magnitude; a head trained on depth error rather than entropy; random pixel dropping; no head; 3 seeds.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: Entropy-trained confidence should give a steeper selective-prediction curve than Laplacian magnitude on the reflective subset. It could fail where specular highlights produce sharp but wrong focus peaks with low entropy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Slice selection policy for short stacks on DDFF
PROPOSAL: Learn a small policy network that picks 5 of 15 slices per scene from a quick low-resolution pass, using DDFF 12-Scene stacks and a base-size ConvNeXt depth network, and compare it against uniform spacing and spacing concentrated near the predicted depth range. Report RMSE and AbsRel for 3 stack lengths, on a low-texture subset and on a reflective subset, and the stability of the chosen slices across reruns of the policy training.
CONTROLS: Uniform spacing; random selection; oracle selection using ground-truth depth; the same depth network fed all 15 slices; 5 seeds.
COST: 150
PREDICTION: The policy should approach the oracle on low-texture scenes and beat uniform spacing at the shortest stack length. It could fail on reflective scenes, where the quick pass misjudges the depth range.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Peak-gated gradient prior for crisp depth edges
PROPOSAL: Train a U-Net with a ConvNeXt-T encoder on FoD500 using a loss that matches the 3x3 Sobel gradient of predicted depth to the gradient of the all-in-focus image, applied only where a single sharp focus peak exists. This keeps texture-induced gradients from being copied into depth. Evaluate RMSE, AbsRel and a bumpiness score on planar regions, plus gradient error at ground-truth depth edges.
CONTROLS: Gradient matching applied at all pixels; no gradient loss; an edge-aware smoothness prior from single-image depth work; a post-hoc bilateral filter on the output; 5 seeds.
COST: 250
PREDICTION: Peak gating should keep edge accuracy close to ungated matching while cutting bumpiness on planar regions. It could fail when peaks are weak across most of the frame, leaving the gate almost always closed.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Guided refinement of coarse depth with the all-in-focus image
PROPOSAL: Predict coarse depth with a ViT-L focal-stack network trained on FoD500, then sharpen it with a learned guided filter driven by the all-in-focus image and the focus-peak sharpness map. Evaluate RMSE, AbsRel, a bumpiness score on planar regions and gradient error at ground-truth depth edges, comparing 3 guide inputs and filter radii of 3, 7 and 15 pixels.
CONTROLS: No refinement; bilateral filtering; refinement guided by RGB only; end-to-end training of the filter with the backbone frozen or unfrozen; 3 seeds.
COST: 250
PREDICTION: A guide that includes sharpness should beat RGB guidance on planar regions without losing edges. It might fail where the sharpness map is noisy, passing that noise into the refined depth.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sensor-noise robustness of learned focus measures
PROPOSAL: Corrupt FoD500 stacks with Poisson-Gaussian noise at 3 levels and train a ViT-B network with a noise-level input that modulates its focus features. Compare against denoising the slices with BM3D and then running the same network. Evaluate RMSE and AbsRel on low-texture regions, where noise most disturbs the focus response, and report depth-edge sharpness at the 3 noise levels.
CONTROLS: No noise conditioning; denoise-first pipeline; a Laplacian focus measure with a matched smoothing window; training at the highest noise level only; 5 seeds.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: Noise conditioning should beat denoise-first at the highest level, because denoising erases the faint focus cues that the network needs. It could fail at the lowest level, where the noise input adds nothing.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Denoising pretraining for a focus encoder
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a ViT-B focus encoder with masked slice reconstruction on stacks from DDFF 12-Scene, FoD500 and DefocusNet corrupted by Poisson-Gaussian noise, and fine-tune on FoD500 for depth. Evaluate RMSE and AbsRel on low-texture regions under 3 noise levels, and measure how much the focus features move from clean to noisy copies of the same stack, using the final encoder layer.
CONTROLS: Random initialisation; ImageNet-pretrained ViT-B; pretraining without noise; fine-tuning on noisy stacks only; 8 seeds.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: Pretraining should shrink the feature shift from clean to noisy copies and help most at high noise. It could fail on DefocusNet, whose synthetic blur differs from sensor noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Focus-distance calibration for metric depth on phone sweeps
PROPOSAL: Learn a per-slice focus-distance embedding with a ResNet-50 backbone on DDFF 12-Scene, where lens parameters are known, and fit a small calibration head that maps the sharpest-slice index to metric depth. Transfer to a smartphone focal sweep set by recalibrating only the head with 20 stacks that carry depth labels. Evaluate AbsRel and RMSE on the sweep set, and the metric-scale error as a function of subject distance.
CONTROLS: No embedding, index-based depth with linear fit; fine-tuning the whole network on the 20 stacks; a monocular metric-depth model with global alignment; 3 seeds.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Head-only recalibration should keep metric scale error low across subject distances. It could fail at far range, where depth of field grows and the focus response flattens.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer of a focus-distance model to phone sweeps by fine-tuning
PROPOSAL: Learn a per-slice focus-distance embedding on DDFF 12-Scene with a Swin-B backbone, and fit a calibration head mapping the sharpest-slice index to metric depth. Transfer to a smartphone focal sweep set by fine-tuning the whole network on 20 labelled stacks, trying 6 learning rates and 4 amounts of trainable layers. Evaluate AbsRel and RMSE on the sweep set, and the metric-scale error as a function of subject distance.
CONTROLS: No embedding, index-based depth with linear fit; head-only recalibration on the 20 stacks; a monocular metric-depth model with global alignment; 5 seeds.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Fine-tuning the whole network may lower scale error at near range but overfit the 20 stacks at far range. It could fail to beat head-only recalibration, since the labelled set is small.
